newsitem.title: ISRAEL: HOT STOCKS - Africa Israel soars.
newsitem.headline: HOT STOCKS - Africa Israel soars.

text.p: Shares in Africa Israel Investments soared the maximum 10 percent on rumours that an investor was looking to purchase shares in the company for the value of $5 million at 15 percent above the market price.
Press reports on Tuesday said that businessmen Motti Zisser and Eitan Wertheimer are to get 200-250 million shekels credit from Bank Hapoalim to purchase shares in Africa Israel.

"Africa is going up as a reaction to the press reports. There are rumours that someone is looking for big packages of stock of Africa outside the bourse. The word is that someone is looking for a package worth $5 million and is prepared to pay 15 percent above market price, " said Ari Eidelhet at Zeler Eblagon Securities.

No comment from Zisser and Wertheimer was available. The two already hold a 6.82 percent stake in Africa Israel. Wertheimer, along with his father Stef, is owner and president of Iscar Ltd, the maker of metal cutting tools. Zisser, president of Control Centres, is a real estate entrepreneur.

Shares in IDB Holdings rose 3.75 percent on speculation that the Wertheimers, with the credit from Bank Hapoalim, would once again start buying shares in IDB in an attempt to force the IDB group to sell its holdings in Iscar, traders said.
IDB, through its subsidiary Discount Investment Corp, owns 25 percent of Iscar, forcing the private Iscar to reveal its earnings so as to be included in IDB's quarterly reports.
Market rumours and press reports said in May that Wertheimer had acquired about 20 percent of shares in IDB.
